items.title: Virus Striker
items.shortDesc: A DirectX 9-based action puzzle game submitted to the 2021 Regional Skills Competition

details.description: An action puzzle game in the style of Qix, reminiscent of the arcade classic 'Gals Panic.' Based on the theme 'Eradicate the Virus!', players control a Vaccine Injection Machine (VIM) to treat infected tissue. The core mechanism uses a FloodFill algorithm where players must fill a certain percentage of the map to clear the stage, avoiding pathogens that increase in difficulty over time. Players must treat the patient within a limited time while evading pathogens.

specs.role: DirectX 9 Framework design and core game system development

keyFeatures: Designed and implemented a 2D rendering engine framework based on DirectX 9
Implemented foundational game engine systems: Animation, Box/Circle Collision, and Sound
Implemented texture masking using 2D array data to distinguish infected and treated areas
Implemented the FloodFill algorithm for area clearing based on 2D array data
Developed a system to parse A-Z and 0-9 sprite sheets to output text without external fonts
Implemented a ranking data I/O system via .txt files
details.review:
'Virus Striker' was the very first game I created while learning C and C++ in high school. This project is more than just a competition entry; it is the project that, for me, marked my first step into the world of game development.

By handling everything from 2D rendering to collision and animation using DirectX APIs, I gained a practical, ground-up understanding of game frameworks and engines. This foundation was immensely helpful when I later transitioned to Unity.

Looking back, 'Virus Striker' might be a simple work in terms of development time, but it is filled with my pure passion and adventurous spirit from that time. Thinking back to those days still evokes a peculiar sense of nostalgia and excitement.

items.title: Corona Striker
items.shortDesc: A vertical-scrolling action shooter submitted to the 2022 Regional Skills Competition

details.description: A vertical-scrolling action shooter similar to 'Strikers 1945.' Set inside a patient's body infected with COVID-19, the player controls a vaccine robot to fight viruses. It features a unique mechanic where players must manage both the robot's health and the patient's pain gauge simultaneously.
keyFeatures: Implemented special skills (Charge Shot) using Bezier Curves
Developed seamless background scrolling using alternating tiles
Configured monster patterns through 2D array data editable in the Unity Inspector
Implemented hit detection and item acquisition logic using Collision handling
details.review:
This was my first Unity project after learning the DirectX graphics API. Having prior experience with low-level APIs proved to be a great asset in understanding the inner workings of the Unity engine.

Since the competition prompt was similar to my previous work 'Virus Striker,' I was able to reuse some assets, but I felt a sense of regret regarding the lack of detail in certain areas. Furthermore, looking at the code I wrote in 2022, I see many instances of hardcoding and immature architectural choices. It is a project I would love to modify or remaster someday.

items.title: Samchuk Adventure
items.shortDesc: A side-scrolling platformer created with Unity for a school performance assessment

details.description: A classic 2D side-scrolling action-adventure game. Players explore forests, dungeons, and caves using various combat styles including swords, spears, bows, and dodge rolls. It includes growth elements like equipment enhancement and shops, requiring players to defeat bosses to reach the ending.

specs.role: Graphics Pipeline management, game mechanics implementation, and providing tool tutorials

keyFeatures: Implemented a system to swap Animators at runtime based on the equipped weapon
Utilized URP 2D Light features to create atmospheric thematic lighting
Implemented camera movement using Cinemachine
Developed equipment enhancement, shop, and dialogue UI using UGUI
Applied Rule Tiles and Gizmos to enhance efficiency in level design
details.review:
This project was my transition from the Built-in pipeline to URP (Universal Render Pipeline). I encountered several hurdles, such as the 'pink texture' bug, but the visual improvement was highly rewarding. 

It was also my first time collaborating with non-programmers. Although I was inexperienced, I took the initiative in schedule management and role distribution. Despite the challenge of developing a game during the school semester, our team produced a work with the highest quality and playability among all competing teams.

While I regret not being able to implement diverse enemy patterns due to time constraints, the experience of learning and applying new features within a two-month period was incredibly exciting and fulfilling.

items.title: LowPoly Battlefield
items.shortDesc: A Low-poly FPS project focused on building 3D development knowledge

details.description: A learning-oriented project to master 3D systems. Focused on customizing external animation assets and exploring Animation Rigging, Animation Curves, and other 3D-specific functionalities to build a solid foundation in 3D game development.
keyFeatures: Implemented gun firing effects using the Particle System
Developed surface-dependent footstep sounds detected via Raycasting
Implemented environmental sound effects including reverb and soundproofing
Developed a JSON-based I/O system for saving customizations
details.review: Although this project concluded at the prototype stage due to technical hurdles in asset optimization and complex 3D mechanics, it was a period of significant growth. I delved deep into FPS fundamentals, such as IK-based animation correction, which greatly enhanced my comprehension of 3D systems. I believe the knowledge gained here will be a cornerstone for my future projects.

items.title: Twin Travelers
items.shortDesc: A 2D co-op puzzle platformer remaster of the 2022 National Skills Competition entry

details.description: A co-op puzzle platformer inspired by 'Fireboy & Watergirl.' Players utilize keys, levers, and gravity portals to overcome obstacles across 50 stages. It supports both a single-player mode (controlling two characters) and real-time network co-op.
keyFeatures: Implemented lag compensation by inheriting Photon PUN2's IPunObservable interface
Developed multiplayer features using Photon PUN2 RPCs and Callbacks
Managed active sound effects using Object Pooling
Managed BGM/SFX lists as Dictionaries using ScriptableObjects
Implemented HDR and Outline effects using Shader Graph
Enhanced level design efficiency using Rule Tiles and Gizmos
details.review:
This project was a major milestone driven by my renewed passion for game development. It wasn't just another attempt; it was a challenge to showcase all the effort and passion I had since the National Skills Competition. 

It is my most ambitious project to date, featuring a successfully implemented multiplayer system using Photon PUN2—a feat I had struggled with in previous attempts. Moving forward, I plan to incorporate UniTask and UniRx to further improve performance and maintainability through event-driven programming.

items.title: Sokoland
items.shortDesc: A 3D reimagining of the classic Sokoban puzzle platformer

details.description: A 3D reimagining of 'Sokoban.' Players use portals, ladders, and camera rotations to place boxes in designated spots. The game challenges spatial awareness through varying themes and complex puzzles that require strategic camera manipulation.

specs.role: Client development, level design, establishing code conventions, and project management

keyFeatures: Implemented player movement and Game Over logic via UniTask and UniRx (Event-driven/Async)
Developed a structured data flow: Theme Data → Level Data → Save Data
Performed per-scene optimization and lighting (Static Batching / Baked Lighting)
Implemented camera rotation using Cinemachine
Developed custom editor scripts for auto-header insertion and per-camera screenshots
details.review:
What started as a simple idea turned into a great experience exploring professional collaboration tools and advanced Unity features. Managing version control via GitHub and overseeing the development schedule taught me the true essence of teamwork. 

I experienced the 'pain of creation' firsthand during level design, but successfully maintaining the workflow was highly rewarding. While my methods for collaboration and management might still differ from industry standards, this project was a vital step in honing the interpersonal and technical skills required for professional development.
